title: Derived, rebuildable SQLite query index at .lore/cache/index.sqlite
description: ODOC-231 Decision §3. Git is the write side; a per-repo, gitignored, rebuildable SQLite index at .lore/cache/index.sqlite is the read model (CQRS/Fossil pattern) - never authoritative, never committed (a merge conflict in a binary SQLite file is unresolvable). Schema follows git-history's design: commits, item, item_version, columns, item_changed, change-only column storage, resumability keyed on commits; add a _mask bitmap of which frontmatter fields changed per version. Index identity is a meta tuple (schema_version, lore_version, indexed_ref, indexed_commit_sha, docs_tree_sha). Staleness is an O(1) tree comparison against git rev-parse HEAD:docs (not commit-based, so it does not churn on commits that never touch docs/). A schema mismatch drops and rebuilds - it never migrates. A stale index is never silently served (exit non-zero or auto-rebuild, and say which). A dirty worktree is indexed as a synthetic uncommitted version, flagged, never conflated with a commit. After indexing a version, re-derive its blob hash and assert it matches. Branches are never modelled as database branches - key rows by commit, scope queries by git merge-base.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A gitignored SQLite index exists at .lore/cache/index.sqlite with a commits/item/item_version/columns/item_changed schema and per-version _mask of changed frontmatter fields
Index identity is a meta tuple (schema_version, lore_version, indexed_ref, indexed_commit_sha, docs_tree_sha); staleness is checked via git rev-parse HEAD:docs tree comparison, O(1)
A schema mismatch triggers drop-and-rebuild, never an in-place migration; a stale index is never silently served
A dirty worktree is represented as a flagged synthetic uncommitted version, never conflated with a real commit
Branches are not modelled as DB rows; queries scope via git merge-base against commit-keyed rows
